newsitem.title: UK: US stocks fall in London, hit by Microsoft.
newsitem.headline: US stocks fall in London, hit by Microsoft.

text.p: U.S. stocks were lower in London trading on Friday, hit by profit taking in the technology sector, signalling a weaker start on Wall Street, dealers said.
The Dow industrials were expected to open about 20 points lower and fall back below the 8,000-point level as investors locked in profits after its record-breaking run this week.
"It's signalling a bit of a pause in the market," one dealer said.
"The market was cushioned yesterday by the big rise in Merck(and Co Inc) so without that there will be more profit taking," he said.
Shares in Merck surged higher on Thursday after reporting slightly higher-than-expected second quarter earnings.
In London, Microsoft traded $4.50 lower at $145 and pressured other technology stocks such at Intel Corp, dealers said.
Microsoft said after the close in New York that fourth-quarter profits rose 88 percent to $1.05 billion, or 80 cents a share, a penny above Wall Street's consensus estimate of 79 cents a share.
Traders said the a sharp rise in the share price over the last week had possibly factored in higher earnings.

Microsoft Chief Financial Officer Mike Brown also said he expected the company's revenues and earnings in the current first quarter to be lower than those just for the fourth quarter that just ended on June 30.
In other London activity, shares in Gillette Co fell about $1 to $100-1/2 after in-line earnings results reported on Thursday sparked some profit taking, dealers said.

On the data front, the U.S. Commerce Department publishes its international trade balance for May at 1230 GMT. Experts surveyed by Reuters are calling for a modest uptick in the trade gap to $9.18 billion from $8.36 billion in April.
